A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MeGan research, with matching authors, core formulation and experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original MeGan benchmark results, component ablations, scaling experiments and qualitative analyses in the main text and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds human evaluations, GPT-4o judgments and experiments progressively zeroing beta dimensions.

M1.justification: The frozen backbone, text-conditioned cross-attention hypernetwork, layer embeddings, beta-SwiGLU gating and training losses remain unchanged. Larger hypernetwork configurations are experimental settings; expanded implementation and caching explanations do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: The represented datasets, task families, ten SNI transfer benchmarks and open-ended emotion examples are retained. GYAFC, MIC and SST already appeared in v1, including dataset-specific baseline training. Their revised training/test descriptions concern existing coverage; the new judging evaluations also reuse these datasets.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds Text-to-LoRA to the CrossFit&UnifiedQA comparison. The domain-specific LoRA and SFT references from v1 Table 11 disappear from the corresponding style comparisons. CoT, PS, MP, CMAML and MLtD are retained in v2 Table 12, rather than removed.

E3.justification: V1 describes GYAFC/MIC/SST as zero-shot tests after SNI training; v2 Table 3 reports dataset-specific training and low-resource evaluation. Task experiments change reported R from 128 to 512, with revised CrossFit learning rates and batch sizes. V2 also revises task-description preprocessing and introduces human/GPT-4o judging protocols. Its ICL description is inconsistent: two shots in Section 6.3 versus three in Appendix B.3. These are documented setting changes, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 7.2 adds a systematic intervention progressively zeroing beta dimensions on SST and non-NLI→NLI, testing their contribution to performance. Appendix C.7 adds all-layer t-SNE analyses for AdaptSum and SST while retaining the GYAFC plots. Conversely, the comparative Persona-Chat overfitting case in v1 Table 14 is removed; the original component ablations remain.

E5.justification: V2 newly specifies four independent human evaluators, discarding the highest and lowest scores before averaging, and two GPT-4o judgments with response order reversed and results averaged. Neither version supplies training-seed uncertainty, confidence intervals or formal significance tests for the main performance comparisons.

E6.justification: Table 5 replaces many MeGan and baseline results: MeGan QA→QA changes from 37.8/57.0 to 72.7/79.5, while HR→LR changes from 72.2/70.9 to 66.7/55.7. Revised settings prevent interpreting these as same-setting gains or losses. V2 adds human/judge results and beta-zeroing curves, and removes domain-specific style baseline scores. The principal persona, domain, style, SNI and Mistral scores otherwise remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The introductory GLU definition broadens from sigmoid gating in v1 Equation 15 to a generic activation in v2 Equation 13. The beta-gradient bound, shifted-beta identity, parameter-count derivation and information-bottleneck argument are retained. The explicit shifted-beta equation expands existing mathematics without adding a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: a lightweight text-conditioned meta-gating framework that adapts activation nonlinearity and generalizes across tasks and conditions. Additional evaluations do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds explicit limitations concerning unseen modalities, acquiring new knowledge and inaccurate conditions, plus a qualitative caching-based latency argument without timing measurements. It distinguishes trained style labels from unseen emotion examples and expands failure interpretations, describing neutral sentiment failures and confusion between desired and current persona states.

D1.justification: V2 adds random instruction-template selection, the GPT-4o task-description generation prompt and examples, baseline learning rates, dataset-specific hypernetwork sizes, and detailed human/judge instructions and aggregation procedures. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation beyond v1. The code link, optimizer, sequence-length limit and hardware disclosure remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds SHINE to the methodological positioning table and discusses a similar context-adaptation architecture; Appendix C.4 additionally mentions ESConv as an emotion-label source. These additions have unresolved question-mark citations. The bibliography itself is unchanged, and neither mention establishes a newly evaluated baseline or dataset.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the appendices into method details (A), implementation/evaluation details (B), and additional results (C), replacing v1's mixed A/B organization. Baseline descriptions and comparisons move between the main text and appendices, while preprocessing, case-analysis and discussion narratives are extensively revised.

P2.justification: V2 consolidates five datasets into Table 4 and secondary comparisons into Table 12. It adds judging tables/figures, an annotation-interface screenshot, beta-zeroing curves and additional layer-wise plot panels. Figure 4 changes from boxplots to violins; case tables are removed or split, and numerous retained displays are relocated.

improvement.justification: Human/GPT-4o evaluations, beta-zeroing experiments and fuller implementation details strengthen evidence about style alignment and gating. However, v2 assigns unchanged style scores a different training interpretation without reconciling the change, removes domain-specific reference baselines, and introduces conflicting two-shot/three-shot ICL descriptions. These issues affect central comparisons enough that the net quality effect cannot be judged reliably despite the useful additions.
